All paths relative to the clone root /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/. Theorem numbers are the compiled ones recorded in scan/map; LaTeX labels given in brackets.

(1) Pointwise2 Lemma 7.3 [co:theta-bridge], preprints/A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-October-7-2026/build/sections/coefficients.tex:256-272 (proof 274-532), verbatim: 'For $\ell$ as in Lemma~\ref{co:kummer}, the reduced modular parametrization followed by $\lambda_M$ admits an integral weighted ternary theta lift. After extraction of the coefficients at multiples of $|h_*|$ it gives a classical holomorphic weight-$3/2$ form $g_M=\sum a_M(n)q^n$, of level supported on $S\cup\{\ell\}$, with \eqref{co:recurrence} modulo $2^M$. The associated characters have $2$-power order and quadratic ratio. For squarefree admissible $D$, $a_M(D)=c_0\,2^{\omega(N)}\zeta_M(D)\lambda_M(\operatorname{red}_\ell(LP_D)) \pmod{2^M}$ [co:weighted-comparison], where $\zeta_M(D)$ is a $2$-power root of unity and $c_0,L$ are fixed integers independent of $D,M,\ell$. The extra index restriction at $\ell$ is $(D/\ell)=1$.' Standing hypotheses (coefficients.tex:12-20, 140-157): $S\supseteq\{2\}\cup\{p\mid N\}$; $F=\mathbb Q(E[2])$ 'trivial or quadratic' (rational 2-torsion); $h_*$ a fixed negative odd fundamental discriminant with $L(E^{(h_*)},1)\ne0$, $|h_*|>4$; $K_D=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{Dh_*})$ 'imaginary, split at $2N$, and has only the units $\{1,-1\}$'; $P_D=\sum_{[\mathfrak a]\in\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal O_{K_D})}\chi_D([\mathfrak a])\varphi(x_D^{[\mathfrak a]})$ the conductor-one genus Heegner sum; all valuations $v(2)=1$. The proof's object (coefficients.tex:275-290): '$B$ ramified at $\ell$ and infinity, $R$ an Eichler order of level $N$ ... The supersingular pairs on $X_0(N)$ are the finite set $X=B^\times\backslash\widehat B^\times/\widehat R^\times$'; the theta series is the full sum over $X$, eq. [co:theta-sum] (447-451): '$H_M(n)=c_0\sum_{z\in X}\frac{P_M(z)\chi_{h_*}(\operatorname{Nrd}z)}{|R_z^\times|}\sum_{x\in B^0,\,Q(x)=n}f(z^{-1}xz)$'.

(1a) Pointwise2 Lemma 7.2 [co:kummer], coefficients.tex:187-207: '$C$ act on $T=T_2E$ as complex conjugation ... For a fixed positive simple-zero witness $D_w$, there are arbitrarily large precisions $M$ and good primes $\ell$ such that $\rho_T(\operatorname{Fr}_\ell)\equiv C\pmod{2^M}$, $(h_*/\ell)=-1$, $(D_w/\ell)=1$ [co:ell-conditions]. Evaluation at Frobenius squared defines an integral homomorphism $\lambda_M:E(\mathbb F_{\ell^2})\to\mathbb Z/2^M\mathbb Z$, $\lambda_M=b\kappa_M$, of Frobenius sign $+1$. The valuation of $\lambda_M(\operatorname{red}_\ell(LP_{D_w}))$ is bounded independently of $M$'; proof ends (251) 'Finally $\det C=-1$ implies $\ell\equiv-1\pmod{2^M}$.'

(1b) Pointwise2 Prop 7.4 [co:odd], coefficients.tex:534-544: 'The forms in Lemma~\ref{co:theta-bridge}, after a fixed adjustment of precision, satisfy $v(a_M(D))\geq\min\{M,j(P_D)-C\}$, $v(a_M(D))<M \Longrightarrow j(P_D)\leq v(a_M(D))+C$. A visible coefficient detects $a(E^{(D)})=1$, and a fixed positive witness has bounded coefficient valuation as $M\to\infty$. All constants are independent of $M,\ell,D$.' ($j(P_D)$ = 'index valuation in the free rational twist line' at a simple zero, 183-185.)

(2) Pointwise2 Prop 7.1 [co:even], coefficients.tex:31-55: 'Fix an even-sign filter and a nonvanishing index $D_0$ in it. There is a holomorphic cuspidal form $g=\sum a(n)q^n$ of weight $3/2$, orthogonal to unary theta series, of level supported on a fixed enlargement of $S$, and characters $\eta,\psi$ of $2$-power order such that $\psi/\eta=\chi_{-\sigma}$ and $a(p^2n)=(\eta(p)a_p(E)-\psi(p)(-n/p))a(n)-p\eta(p)^2a(n/p^2)$ $(p\notin S)$ ... For two nonzero squarefree coefficients, $2v(a(D)/a(D_0))=v(L_*(\sigma D)/L_*(\sigma D_0))$ [co:exact-ratio]. Moreover $a(D)\neq0$ exactly when $L(E^{(\sigma D)},1)\neq0$. Consequently any previously established bound $v(L_*(\sigma D))\geq2w(D)+s(\sigma D)-C$ gives $v(a(D))\geq w(D)+\tfrac12 s(\sigma D)-C_g$.' Goldfeld2 Prop 4.1 [prop:even-coefficients], preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/build/sections/05-coefficients.tex:52-94, is the same statement (items (i)-(iii), eqs. cs:hecke-recurrence, cs:even-ratio, cs:even-value, cs:even-lower-bound) with the filter defined at 05-coefficients.tex:14-27.

(3) Goldfeld2 Prop 4.2 [prop:odd-coefficients], 05-coefficients.tex:270-318: 'Assume that a constant $C_*$ satisfies $j(P_D)\geq w(D)+\tfrac12 s(h)-C_*$ [cs:odd-bound-hypothesis] for every $h$ in the filter with a simple zero. There are arbitrarily large precisions $M$, good odd primes $\ell$ outside the fixed support, and holomorphic weight-$3/2$ forms $g_M=\sum a_M(n)q^n$, of level supported on $S\cup\{\ell\}$, with the following properties. (i) The additional filter at $\ell$ is $(h_*/\ell)=-\sigma$, $(h/\ell)=\sigma$, $\rho_T(\Fr_\ell)\equiv C\pmod{2^M}$ [cs:detecting-prime] ... In particular $\ell\equiv-1\pmod{2^M}$. (ii) ... the forms satisfy Equation~\eqref{cs:hecke-recurrence} modulo that precision ... (iii) If a coefficient is visible, meaning $v(a_M(D))<M$, then $E^{(h)}$ has a simple zero and $j(P_D)\leq v(a_M(D))+C_1$ [cs:odd-detection]. For every admissible $D$ the coefficient lower bound is $v(a_M(D))\geq\min\{M,w(D)+\tfrac12 s(h)-C_2\}$ [cs:odd-lower-bound] when the product derivative is nonzero; if it is zero, the coefficient is zero modulo $2^M$. ... (iv) A fixed squarefree witness $D_w$ ... has $v(a_M(D_w))$ bounded as $M\to\infty$. For irreducible $E[2]$, the hypothesis is Theorem~\ref{thm:heegner-genus-bound}. For rational two-torsion, the positive filters used in the pointwise argument have this bound by Proposition~\ref{prop:rational-odd-bound}'. Key identity (proof, 628-633) [cs:weighted-trace-identity]: '$a_M(D)=c_0\,2^{\omega(N)}\zeta_M(D)\,\lambda_M(\operatorname{red}_\ell(LP_D))\pmod{2^M}$'. Standing: $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt k)$ with 'every prime dividing $2N$ splits in $K$. We omit the two fields with extra units and, if $E$ has complex multiplication, its CM field' (01-arithmetic-transfer.tex:112-114).

(4) Goldfeld2 Prop 8.2 [prop:selmer-matrix-bound], preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/build/sections/09-local-matrices.tex:262-277: 'Fix the curve, support types, a bound for the number of additional constrained places, and a bound for the dimension of a stationary environment. Partition a finite configuration into blocks with zero cross-$M$ entries, and denote their matrices by $M_i$. There is a constant depending only on these fixed data such that $\dim_{\F_2}\Sel_2(E^{(h)}/\Q)\geq\sum_i\dim_{\F_2}\ker M_i-C$ [eq:lm:selmer-nullity]. At a unit coefficient symbol the sum of nullities, and hence the number of singular blocks, is therefore uniformly bounded. The bound works for both coefficient sources and is independent of the moving prime $\ell$.'

(5) Goldfeld2 Prop 3.8 [prop:rough-nonvanishing], preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/build/sections/01-arithmetic-transfer.tex:335-359: 'Let $E/\Q$ have conductor $N$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes containing the prime divisors of $2N$. Prescribe a real sign $\sigma$ and a unit squareclass $c_p$ for each $p\in S$. Suppose that these data are realized by an odd fundamental discriminant, and that twists in this filter have root number $\varepsilon$. For every finite set $B$ of primes there are odd fundamental discriminants $D$ of arbitrarily large absolute value such that $\operatorname{sign}(D)=\sigma$, $[D]_p=c_p$ $(p\in S)$, $p\nmid D$ $(p\in B)$. Moreover: (i) If $\varepsilon=1$, they can be chosen with $L(E^{(D)},1)\ne0$ and $\omega(|D|)\le5$. (ii) If $\varepsilon=-1$, they can be chosen with $L'(E^{(D)},1)\ne0$'. Pointwise2 Props 6.1 [nv:local-witness] and 6.2 [nv:rough], preprints/A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-October-7-2026/build/sections/nonvanishing.tex:9-26, are the same existence statements ('one can require $\omega(d)\le A_0$').

(6) H10Q Lemma 3.4 [par:descent], preprints/Hilberts-tenth-problem-over-the-rational-numbers-October-6-2026/build/sections/03-parity.tex:300-314: 'Let $l>0$ be squarefree, prime to $6$, with $l\equiv3\pmod4$ and $l\equiv2\pmod3$. Suppose that its support $Q$ contains the nonempty set $B$ of Lemma~\ref{par:cross-squares} and a prime outside $B$, and suppose that $\ker K=\langle\mathbf1,\mathbf1_B\rangle$, $\lambda\notin\operatorname{im}K$. Then $\dim_{\F_2}\Sel_2(E_l/\Q)=3$, and $(\beta,1)$ is a Selmer class outside the subgroup of rational two-torsion classes, in Kummer coordinates $(x+3l,x-l)$.' ($E_l: y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l)$, full rational 2-torsion.)

(7) ExactBSD Prop 5.2 [single:siegel-traces], preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/build/sections/05-single.tex:132-150: 'The classes just constructed are integral away from $pn_2\infty$ and compatible with division traces and with corestriction as the $p$-part of $M$ grows with $A,c,d,\xi$ fixed. If $\ell\nmid cdn_2L_0$ is a fresh prime and is adjoined to both orders and the root index, the rational norm multiplier is $1-\frac{a_\ell(f)[\ell]}{\ell}+\frac{[\ell]^2}{\ell}$ [single:good-norm] ... filling $q_0^a$ into the first row gives, at a finite even character $\nu$, $z_{\rm filled}=(1-a_{q_0}(f)\nu(q_0)/q_0)z_{\rm before}$ [single:bad-row].' Prop 5.4 [single:period-law], 05-single.tex:299-311: 'In square or unfilled rectangular order, for every finite even character $\nu$ of conductor dividing $M$, the coordinate of $\exp^*(z_\nu)$ in $\omega$, in compatible field realizations, is $\pm\Delta_\nu\frac{L^{(M)}(f,\nu,1)}{\Omega_0}\delta_\xi(a)$, $\Delta_\nu=(c^2-c\nu(c)^{-1})(d^2-d\nu(d)^{-1})$ [eq:source-2]'. Prop 6.1 [pair:primitive], preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/build/sections/06-pair.tex:84-106: 'On the canonical ordinary locus define $f^{[p]}=(1-a_pV_p+p\epsilon_pV_p^2)f$, $F_0=\lim_{j\to\infty}d_{\rm mod}^{(p-1)p^j-1}f^{[p]}$, $F=\prod_{q\in S^\circ}P_q(V_q)F_0$. The limits are integral weight-zero functions ... If $z$ is a Serre--Tate coordinate with $z=1$ at the canonical lift, the expansion $F(z)$ is the transform of a bounded integral measure $\mu$ on $\Z_p$, supported on $\Z_p^\times$. On every interior CM disk one has the exact identity $F_0=P_p(V_p)G$ [eq:source-9].' Standing for Section 6 (06-pair.tex:3-7, 36-38): '$p=w\bar w$ in $K$, every rational prime below the fixed finite support for $E/K$ splits in $K$'; '$S^\circ$ ... These primes split in $K$.'

(8) SelmerConverse Lemma 2.3 [lem:auxiliary-fields], preprints/The-Selmer-converse-for-elliptic-curves-at-every-prime-October-7-2026/build/sections/02-reduction.tex:78-93: 'There are coprime negative odd fundamental discriminants $D,D'$ such that every prime dividing $2Np$ splits in both quadratic fields, $(D/|D'|)=1$, and each of $A_0^D,A_0^{D'},A_0^{DD'}$ has the smallest analytic rank permitted by its sign. ... $L/F$ is CM and unramified at every finite prime, $L$ has only the roots of unity $\{\pm1\}$, and $L$ does not contain the CM field of $A_0$'. Lemma 4.1 [lem:split-u-operators], 04-theta-construction.tex:221-226: 'Every test \eqref{eq:p-pivot-test} satisfies $U_2\Phi_p=p^2\Phi_p$ and $U_3\Phi_p=p^2\Phi_p$'; Prop 4.3 [prop:theta-family], 286-303: 'For the characters \eqref{eq:theta-character} and every sufficiently large positive $m$ on the prescribed branch, the theta construction gives holomorphic algebraic forms $\Theta_{i,m}$ of weight \eqref{eq:theta-weight}. In the canonical ordinary monomial-dual lattice their coefficients have a common bounded denominator ... They have spherical parameters \eqref{eq:theta-eigenparameters}, and at both distinguished $p$-places they satisfy $p^{-2}U_2\Theta_{i,m}=\Theta_{i,m}$, $p^{-2}U_3\Theta_{i,m}=\Theta_{i,m}$.' (forms on a unitary group over a real quadratic $F$ with $p$ split in $K$).

(9) Repository-wide items (scan/map/sweep-overview.json findings[2],[3]; sweep-lean.json findings[2]): family 142 Thm 1.1 deterministic $\F_p$ factorization in $O(((n+1)\lceil\log_2 p\rceil)^{10^{12}})$ bit operations; family 107 Thm 1.1 $\omega\le9/4$; 109 integer multiplication $O(n(\lg n)^{1-2^{-182}})$; 130 DFT $O(n(\log n)^{1-10^{-13}})$; Lean OAI/NumberTheory/SingleFold/{DescentMap,Rank,Torsion}.lean: 2-descent on $y^2=x^3-25x$ ('theorem rank_one', 'kummer_eq_zero_iff'), uncatalogued in lean/formalization.yaml.
hypotheses_check:
Seed data used: E rank 2, N=2^3*3*2243*4547^2*5843, E(Q)_tors=Z/2 (so F=Q(E[2]) is quadratic, E[2] reducible), w(E)=+1, L(E,1)=L'(E,1)=0, Sha[2^inf]=0, Sha[3^inf]=(Z/3)^2; K=Q(sqrt-7) with 2, 4547 split and 3, 2243, 5843 inert; E^{-7} rank 0, L(E^{-7},1) in [9.054319, 9.054421] != 0, root number +1, conductor 49N.

A. Theta-bridge / odd detector (Pointwise2 Lemma 7.2, 7.3, Prop 7.4; Goldfeld2 Prop 4.2). Hypotheses: (H1) coefficient prime 2 (T=T_2E, precision 2^M, v(2)=1) - holds trivially but is the WRONG prime for every open seed obligation (Sha[2^inf]=0 is done). (H2) the detected object is the genus Heegner sum P_D of a TWIST E^{(D)} with a SIMPLE zero over K_D=Q(sqrt(D h_*)) split at 2N - K-RANK2: E itself is D=1 in the even-sign filter (w(E)=+1), where Prop 7.1/4.1 says a(1)!=0 iff L(E,1)!=0; L(E,1)=0 so a(1)=0 and the even detector is silent on E; D=1 is not in any odd-sign filter, so the odd detector never sees E. Rank 2 is exactly outside 'simple zero'. (H3) Heegner hypothesis 'every prime dividing 2N splits in K_D': the lab's K=Q(sqrt-7) FAILS at 3, 2243, 5843 (inert); -7=D h_* would need D h_* with all of 2,3,2243,4547,5843 split; the manuscripts choose their own varying K_D and never touch Q(sqrt-7). (H4) rational 2-torsion (Pointwise2) - holds (E(Q)[2]=Z/2); irreducible E[2] (Goldfeld2 Thm 3.6 branch) - fails; Goldfeld2's rational-torsion branch via Prop rational-odd-bound would apply formally. (H5) auxiliary ell: good odd prime, ell = -1 mod 2^M, rho_T(Fr_ell) = C mod 2^M - an auxiliary DETECTOR prime, not a prime at which anything about Sha(E) is concluded. (H6) h_* with L(E^{(h_*)},1)!=0, |h_*|>4 - h_*=-7 is a candidate (L(E^{-7},1)!=0, PROVED_COMPUTER_ASSISTED) but 7 then enters the fixed support S and is excluded from variable indices; it still does not make K_D=Q(sqrt(-7D)) satisfy the split condition at 3,2243,5843 for any D. Prime by prime for the seed: p=2: coefficient prime, obligation already closed. p=3, 2243, 5843 (multiplicative), 4547 (additive III), 2 (I1*): all in S as level primes; the construction only imposes 'split fundamental unit squareclass' and Atkin-Lehner signs w_{p^e} at p^e || N (coefficients.tex:306-339) and allows 'arbitrary depth at 2'; it produces NO statement about Sha(E)[p^inf] at any of these p. Good ordinary / good supersingular p >= 5: the only good prime that appears is the detector ell (ell = -1 mod 2^M, inert in Q(sqrt(h_*))); no output at any good target prime. rho-bar surjectivity: not required (the manuscripts use Faltings 1983 / Serre 1968 irreducibility of V_2 E plus Bogomolov's homothety for the 2-adic Tate module, which hold for every non-CM curve); irrelevant for the seed because no conclusion is drawn at an odd p.

B. Even coefficient system (Pointwise2 Prop 7.1 / Goldfeld2 Prop 4.1). Hypotheses: even-sign filter with a nonvanishing index D_0 (exists by Prop 3.8 / 6.1, or take sigma D_0 = -7); Waldspurger (H1)/(H2) handled as described. For E (D=1): a(1)=0 since L(E,1)=0 - nothing. For E^{-7} (h=-7, root number +1, L(E^{-7},1)!=0): formally applicable; output is 2 v_2(a(D)/a(D_0)) = v_2(L_*(sigma D)/L_*(sigma D_0)), i.e. 2-adic valuations of algebraic central values of twists in the filter, which the lab can compute directly from L-values (and already has L(E^{-7},1) to 7 digits); it yields #Sha(E^{-7})[2^inf] only if BSD for E^{-7} is assumed (K-A), and the cyclotomic lower bound (Thm 3.1) has an ineffective constant C_E.

C. Goldfeld2 Prop 8.2 (2-Selmer lower bound via block nullities): requires the whole configuration machinery (sites, stationary environment, type sums) built for twists E^{(h)} in a filter; gives a LOWER bound on dim_{F_2} Sel_2(E^{(h)}), the opposite direction from what any seed obligation needs (upper bounds / vanishing at odd p); its 'unit symbol' input is the ultrafilter-defined odd symbol (05-coefficients.tex:683-699). Not applicable to E (rank 2, no filter index) nor useful for E^{-7}.

D. H10Q Lemma 3.4: curve family y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l) with full rational 2-torsion, l = 3 mod 4, l = 2 mod 3, plus Redei-matrix conditions. The seed has E(Q)[2]=Z/2 only (not full 2-torsion), is not of this shape, and the statement is about 2-Selmer of that family. Fails.

E. ExactBSD Props 5.2/5.4 (Kato classes, norm relation, reciprocity): hypotheses are Kato's (f the seed newform, odd p, level data n_2, Rohrlich's theorem for the rectangular case); formally applicable to the seed's f at any odd p, but they are re-normalizations of Kato 2004 Sections 8-9, 13 with no algorithm; the lab already imports Kato directly. Prop 6.1 (integral logarithmic primitive / measure on Z_p^x): requires (06-pair.tex:3-7, 36-38) p = w w-bar SPLIT in K and every prime of the fixed support for E/K split in K; for K=Q(sqrt-7): fails at 3, 2243, 5843 (inert) and at every good inert p; holds only at good split p (p = 2,4547 split but 2 is excluded as 'odd prime' and 4547 is a bad prime). So Prop 6.1 is unusable for the lab's K at the bad primes and at inert good primes (the supersingular-inert case the lab cares about, cf. SEED_CONTEXT update on Shii).

F. SelmerConverse Lemma 2.3 / Lemma 4.1 / Prop 4.3: Lemma 2.3 chooses NEW fields D, D' with 2Np split (so K=Q(sqrt-7) can never be the output); Lemma 4.1 / Prop 4.3 are U(3,1)-theta forms over a real quadratic F with p split in K; p inert in K is excluded. Fails for 3, 2243, 5843 and all inert good p; no algorithm in any case.

G. Nonvanishing existence (Pointwise2 6.1/6.2, Goldfeld2 3.8, SelmerConverse 2.3): existence of some D with L(E^{(D)},1)!=0 or L'!=0 in a filter; no explicit D; the seed already has the explicit witness -7 (and published theorems Murty-Murty 1991, Bump-Friedberg-Hoffstein 1990, Ono-Skinner 1998 give existence).

H. Galactic complexity results and the Lean 2-descent: no hypothesis is at issue; they do not touch the seed's named computations (see what_lab_must_do).
